steps.title: Fission heat in the HTGR core
text: Inside the core, uranium nuclei in the TRISO fuel particles split when they absorb a neutron, and the graphite slows the new neutrons so the chain reaction carries on.
The fission heat passes to helium flowing through the core, which leaves at 925°C. The reactor runs at 177.6MWth of its 210MWth rating.
notes: The design basis is a generic 925°C HTGR. No commercial reactor runs at this outlet, and Xe-100 is only a labelled analogue with a much lower outlet temperature.

inset.label: Illustration: inside a TRISO fuel particle in graphite, a neutron splits a uranium nucleus into two fragments and new neutrons, and the heat passes to the helium flowing past.
inset.cap: Illustration. The engine models the reactor as a heat source and holds no fuel, neutron or core data.
svgText: a neutron splits a uranium nucleus
helium carries the heat out of the core

steps.title: Primary helium loop
text: Hot primary helium at 925°C passes 121.5MW to a separate secondary loop in the intermediate heat exchanger (IHX), so the reactor coolant never enters the chemical plant.
The circulator sends the cooled helium back to the core.
notes: A branch of the hot helium also runs to the power block, which step 12 follows.

steps.title: Secondary helium loop to the reformer
text: The secondary helium leaves the IHX at 900°C, heats the reformer tubes and returns at 466°C, bringing 120.8MWth of process heat that a conventional reformer would raise by burning natural gas.
A second circulator on the return leg draws 3.48MWe; the drawing does not show it.
notes: The helium connections on the reformer are drawn schematically. In the engine's tube model the hot helium enters at the process gas outlet end and flows against the process gas.
Input outside its evidence range: Helium supply temperature is fixed at 900 C. Highest measured secondary helium temperature is 859 C, HTTR 2004 high-temperature run (IAEA NP-T-4.3 printed p.14).

steps.title: Natural gas and steam feed the reformer
text: Natural gas at 23.2MMSCFD and process steam enter the reformer, joined by the methane-rich recycle of step 9. In the catalyst tubes methane and steam react to hydrogen and carbon monoxide, taking up the helium's heat.
The engine sets the exit at 871°C, INL's equilibrium assumption; with helium at 900°C, the tube model reaches only 782.1°C (precomputed) on the assumed tube.

steps.title: Water-gas shift
text: The syngas raises steam as it leaves the reformer and enters the high-temperature shift bed at 335°C.
Over the shift catalyst, carbon monoxide and steam form more hydrogen and carbon dioxide, and the beds release 8.0MW of heat.
eq: Reaction, for illustrationCO + H₂O ⇌ CO₂ + H₂
notes: The drawing shows the two beds, and the coolers between them, as one vessel.

text: In the packed absorber the gas rises against falling 30wt% aqueous monoethanolamine (MEA) at 22.0bar.
The amine takes up 92.0% of the CO₂ in one pass and leaves at the bottom as rich solvent; the hydrogen-rich gas leaves at the top.
eq: Reaction, for illustrationCO₂ + 2 RNH₂ ⇌ RNHCOO⁻ + RNH₃⁺

steps.title: PSA reject back to the cryogenic unit
text: The PSA reject, still holding 1,226kg/h of hydrogen, crosses back into the boundary and is compressed for the cryogenic unit.
The cold separation returns hydrogen to the PSA feed and a methane-rich recycle to the reformer. The nitrogen-rich cut is burned and leaves by the stack as the plant's residual 29,468t/y of CO₂.
notes: CO₂ slip into this unit is about ten times INL's, and freeze-out and reverse shift are unquantified, so INL's recycle may not transfer to MEA.
The burner of the nitrogen-rich cut is not drawn; the stack stands for it.

steps.title: Stripper and reboiler heat
text: Rich solvent is warmed in the rich/lean exchanger and stripped at 1.5bar by reboiler steam, which drives the CO₂ out; the lean solvent is cooled and pumped back to the absorber.
The reboiler needs 56.8MW, met in a fixed order: freed Selexol steam 12.7MW, export steam 16.8MW, syngas heat 8.4MW, and reactor steam 18.9MW last.
notes: No line on the drawing brings heat into the reboiler; the order comes from the engine's energy balance.

steps.title: CO₂ compression, ship and offshore storage
text: The condenser returns water from the stripper overhead as reflux, and the CO₂ is compressed to 138.9bar (precomputed) using 4.28MWe.
Then 298,368t/y of CO₂ leaves by ship for storage offshore abroad, which the model treats as a tariff of 100S$/t with no simulation.
notes: How offshore storage abroad counts as abatement is unresolved.

inset.label: Illustration: a ship carries the compressed CO₂ from the plant to an offshore store, where it goes into a rock formation deep under the seabed.
inset.cap: Illustration. The engine models the ship and the store as a tariff only.

steps.title: The plant from end to end
text: End to end, the plant makes 55,114t/y of purified hydrogen and sends 298,368t/y of CO₂ to storage.

Against the 507,591t/y an unabated reformer would emit on INL's baseline, its residual of 29,468t/y leaves a net abatement of 478,123t/y. Part of that is the CO₂ stored; the rest is never formed, since no natural gas is burned for reformer heat.
The abatement target of 250,000t/y is met at these inputs. On Cho's and IEAGHG's baselines the net abatement is 485,852t/y and 466,341t/y.
status: Cost target: Not met at these inputs: L5 258.1 S$/t and DCF 258.5 S$/t against the 100 S$/t target at the selected stage, life, exponent and size charged.
notes: The plant sits on the proposed Western Island site, a proposal of this study with no official approval.
